authority: diagnostic: paper only, not investment advice
flags: Ingevity completed the sale of its North Charleston crude tall oil refinery and the majority of its industrial specialties product line to Mainstream Pine Products, LLC.

Ingevity announced the completion of its Strategic Portfolio Review and the exploration of strategic alternatives for its Advanced Polymer Technologies reportable segment, and continues to advance a sale of Advanced Polymer Technologies.
Ingevity completed the sale of its former Performance Chemicals' road markings product line to PPG Industries Inc. for all-cash proceeds of $63.2 million.

business_model.basis: stated in S0, P1, and P4
business_model.claim: Ingevity Corporation is a United States specialty chemicals company in the basic materials sector that develops, manufactures, and sells largely renewably sourced products and technologies for automotive emissions control, filtration, asphalt paving, agrochemical dispersants, bioplastics, coatings, and elastomers.
quotes: Through a diverse team of talented and experienced people, we develop, manufacture, and bring to market solutions that are largely renewably sourced and help customers solve complex problems while making the world more sustainable.

Our products are used in a variety of demanding applications, including automotive gasoline vapor emissions control systems, food, water and chemical filtration, asphalt paving, agrochemical dispersants, bioplastics, coatings, and elastomers.

business_model.claim: In 2025, Ingevity sold products to customers in approximately 70 countries, with customers outside the U.S. accounting for approximately 43 percent of total sales, its ten largest customers accounting for 41 percent of total sales, no single customer exceeding 10 percent, and business with large customers resting primarily on individual purchase orders.
quotes: In 2025, sales to customers outside of the U.S. made up approximately 43 percent of our total sales, and we sell our products to customers in approximately 70 countries.
Sales to the Company's ten largest customers (across all three segments) accounted for 41 percent of total sales for 2025.
No customer accounted for more than 10 percent of total sales for 2025.
With some exceptions, our business with those large customers is based primarily upon individual purchase orders.

business_model.claim: Following the completed divestitures of its North Charleston crude tall oil refinery and most of its industrial specialties product line, and the sale of its road markings product line for $63.2 million, Ingevity operates in three reportable segments: Performance Materials, Pavement Technologies, and Advanced Polymer Technologies.
quotes: On September 4, 2025, we announced the agreement to sell the North Charleston crude tall oil refinery and the majority of the industrial specialties product line, and on January 1, 2026, the announced sale was completed.

We received all-cash proceeds of $63.2 million, inclusive of preliminary traditional working capital adjustments, and recorded an incremental loss of $3.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, which resulted in a gain of $5.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.
We operate in three reportable segments: Performance Materials, Pavement Technologies and Advanced Polymer Technologies.

business_model.claim: Ingevity is advancing a potential sale of its Advanced Polymer Technologies segment, with the timing of an announced agreement potentially extending into early 2027, to leave a portfolio focused on Performance Materials and Pavement Technologies.
quotes: New Ingevity will be comprised of two attractive businesses aligned around strong core competencies, with superior and consistent profitability: Performance Materials and Pavement Technologies.
We also continue to advance the sale of Advanced Polymer Technologies, however, the timing of an announced agreement may extend into early 2027.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P2, and P6
business_model.claim: Performance Materials sells automotive activated carbon and extruded honeycomb products tied to global internal combustion and hybrid vehicle production as well as non-auto filtration products for chemicals, food, and water, generating $470.1 (table in millions) in net sales and $261.5 (table in millions) in Segment EBITDA during the first nine months of 2026 and a 54.1% Segment EBITDA margin in the third quarter of 2026.
quotes: Sales of our automotive activated carbon products are tied to global internal combustion engine ("ICE") and hybrid electric vehicle automobile ("HEV") production levels.

Performance Materials net sales remained strong and nearly flat to prior year at $154.1 million as resilient North American demand, supported by continued consumer preference for hybrid vehicles, and higher non-auto filtration sales driven primarily by pricing, offset lower volumes from softness in automotive applications in China and Europe.
Segment EBITDA margin remained strong at 54.1%, consistent with the prior year, demonstrating the resilient earnings power of the segment.

business_model.basis: stated in P1, P2, and P6
business_model.claim: Pavement Technologies provides asphalt paving products for construction, preservation, reconstruction, and recycling to customers who primarily provide paving services to governments in North America, South America, Europe, China, Brazil, and India, generating 268.5 (table in $ millions) in net sales and 45.6 (table in $ millions) in Segment EBITDA during the first nine months of 2026 (including road markings prior to its sale).
quotes: While we do not do business directly with governmental agencies in our pavement technologies product line, our customers provide paving services to the governments of various jurisdictions within North America, South America, Europe, China, Brazil and India, and revenue either directly or indirectly attributable to such government spending continues to remain a significant portion of our revenues.
Pavement Technologies net sales decreased 24% to $106.0 million, primarily due to the April 15, 2026, divestiture of the Road Markings product line.

business_model.claim: Advanced Polymer Technologies sells caprolactone-based polymers and derivative products into automotive, industrial equipment, footwear and apparel, bioplastics, consumer packaging, coatings, elastomers, and medical and health markets, generating 138.6 (table in $ millions) in net sales during the first nine months of 2026 and $45.0 million in net sales and $11.7 million in Segment EBITDA in the third quarter of 2026.
quotes: The superior durability of caprolactone-based polyurethane technologies extends product life, and the biodegradable performance of our thermoplastic polycaprolactones offers compostable end-of-life solutions.

Advanced Polymer Technologies net sales increased 18% to $45.0 million driven by higher pricing, including a price surcharge to offset increased input costs, and favorable mix toward higher-value derivative products.
Segment EBITDA for the quarter increased $0.7 million to $11.7 million, primarily driven by the favorable product mix and higher pricing partially offset by higher input costs.

business_model.claim: At the consolidated level, net sales in the first nine months of 2026 decreased by $35.3 million from the prior year, as a $68.2 million volume decrease largely driven by the road markings divestiture outweighed $29.3 million in favorable pricing and sales mix and $3.6 million in favorable foreign currency exchange.
quotes: The Net sales decrease of $35.3 million in 2026 was driven by a volume decrease of $68.2 million (seven percent), partially offset by favorable pricing and sales mix of $29.3 million (three percent) and favorable foreign currency exchange of $3.6 million (zero percent).

Excluding the road markings disposition, sales increased two percent from the prior year driven by higher pricing and favorable mix across the portfolio, partially offset by lower volumes in Performance Materials and Pavement Technologies.

business_model.basis: stated in P2, P3, and P6
business_model.claim: End-market demand and competition move segment revenue differently: automotive carbon faces electric vehicle adoption and sealed fuel-tank systems that generally do not use extruded honeycombs, Pavement Technologies faces government funding shifts and crude oil-driven asphalt inflation that raises customer project costs, and APT faces cyclical industrial demand and competition from Chinese and substitute producers.
quotes: While sealed tank fuel systems generally require an increased sized pelleted activated carbon canister to deal with refueling emissions, in most cases, they do not use an extruded honeycomb to meet current U.S. and California regulations.

A significant portion of our customers' revenues in our pavement technologies is derived from contracts with various foreign and U.S. governmental agencies, and therefore, when government spending is reduced, our customers' demand for our products is similarly reduced.
Persistently higher asphalt costs, driven by crude oil inflation, continued to increase project costs for our customers, pressuring demand and limiting sales growth.

The Net sales decrease of $32.5 million was driven primarily by the APT reportable segment as continued weak industrial demand, indirect tariff impacts negatively impacted customer end markets demand and increased China competition pressured sales.

business_model.claim: Pavement technologies revenue is seasonal, with roughly 70 to 75 percent generated between April and September, and prolonged or severe wet weather can delay projects and reduce demand.
quotes: There are a variety of seasonal dynamics, including global climate and weather conditions, that impact our businesses, though none have currently materially affected our financial results, except in the case of the pavement technologies and road markings product lines, where roughly 70 to 75 percent of revenue is generated between April and September.

Furthermore, our Performance Chemicals pavement technologies and road markings product lines financial results can be sensitive to weather conditions, particularly prolonged or severe wet weather, which can disrupt operations, delay projects, and reduce customer demand across certain markets.

business_model.claim: Trade policy changes and tariffs, including U.S. global tariffs and retaliatory tariffs from trading partners such as China, increase export and import costs and can compress margins or reduce customer demand.
quotes: These changes to trade policy are expected to make it more difficult or costly for us to export our products and import raw materials.

The retaliatory tariff measures imposed by China, if not unwound, may significantly lower our margin on Performance Materials and Performance Chemicals products sold from the United States into China if we are unable to pass these costs onto our customers.

business_model.claim: Production costs depend on third-party raw materials—including hardwood sawdust, phosphoric acid, ethylene amines, tall oil fatty acid, lignin, maleic/fumaric acid, hydrogen peroxide, cyclohexanone, and ethoxylates—and can rise when raw material supply (such as lignin and tall oil fatty acid) tightens or when input and logistics costs inflate faster than price surcharges recover them.
quotes: The Company purchases a variety of raw materials from third parties for its manufacturing operations, including, but not limited to, hardwood sawdust, phosphoric acid, ethylene amines, tall oil fatty acid ("TOFA"), lignin, maleic/fumaric acid, hydrogen peroxide, cyclohexanone, and ethoxylates.

For example, lignin and TOFA are in limited supply and if we are unable to secure a sufficient amount of lignin or TOFA on a cost-effective basis we could suffer disruption to our pavement technologies product line, which could negatively impact our financial results and our results of operations.

Favorable pricing and product mix, strong operating performance in Performance Materials and improved results in Advanced Polymer Technologies partially offset higher input and logistics costs in Pavement Technologies and Advanced Polymer Technologies.

business_model.claim: Manufacturing operations consume significant natural gas (hedged with derivatives against market price volatility) and electricity, rely on third-party utilities at co-located plants in Covington, Virginia and Warrington, U.K., produce several key products at single sites, and employ unionized workers representing approximately 52 percent of production employees.
quotes: We depend on natural gas to power the processes in our activated carbon plants and chemical manufacturing operations.
We enter into certain derivative financial instruments to mitigate expected fluctuations in market prices and the resulting volatility of earnings and cash flow.
Approximately 52 percent of our production employees are represented by labor unions under various collective bargaining agreements ("CBA").

We are dependent upon third parties for the provision of certain critical operating services, primarily utilities and related services (depending on the site, e.g., compressed air, energy, water, wastewater treatment, hydrogen peroxide), at our plants in Covington, Virginia, and Warrington, United Kingdom.

In certain cases, we have products, such as our extruded honeycomb, caprolactone, pavement preservation products, road construction products, pavement reconstruction and recycling products, that are only made at a single site, such as our Waynesboro, Georgia Performance Materials plant, North Charleston Performance Chemicals plant and Warrington, U.K. APT plant.

business_model.claim: Restructuring under the Performance Chemicals Repositioning Actions captured approximately $105 million in cash savings—roughly 75 percent in cost of sales, 20 percent in SG&A, and 5 percent in research and technical expenses—plus approximately $12 million in lower annual depreciation and amortization, though Pavement Technologies absorbed retained dis-synergy costs after the road markings divestiture.
quotes: Inclusive of continuing and discontinued operations, since November of 2023, we have realized approximately $105 million in cash savings.
In addition to the cash savings, we realized approximately $12 million in lower full year depreciation and intangible amortization expenses.
Segment EBITDA reflects lower volumes, the retention of dis-synergy costs largely due to the divestiture of road markings, as well as higher input and logistics costs.

business_model.claim: In the first nine months of 2026, continuing operations recorded $877.2 (table in millions) of net sales against 489.0 (table in $ millions) of cost of sales, $117.8 million of SG&A, 21.1 (table in $ millions) of research and technical expenses, 32.1 (table in $ millions) of long-lived asset impairment, and 43.6 (table in $ millions) of net interest expense, producing 114.3 (table in $ millions) of net income from continuing operations.
quotes: SG&A was $117.8 million (13 percent of Net sales) and $129.6 million (14 percent of Net sales) for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

Research and technical expenses as a percentage of Net sales remained relatively consistent period over period, totaling 2.4 percent and 2.3 percent for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively.

business_model.basis: stated in F3, P1, P4, P5, and P6
business_model.claim: Ingevity relies on patents, trademarks, and trade secrets to protect its competitive position, and IP litigation and related antitrust counterclaims resulted in a 16.2 (table in $ millions) litigation charge and a $113.2 million litigation settlement payment during the first nine months of 2026.
quotes: Protection of intellectual property, including patents, closely guarded trade secrets, and highly proprietary manufacturing know-how, as well as other proprietary rights, is critical to maintaining our technology leadership and competitive edge.

Any legal actions to protect, defend or enforce our intellectual property rights could result in significant costs and diversion of our resources and our management's attention, and we may not prevail in any such other actions, which could have an adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.

competitive_position.claim: Ingevity states that its Performance Materials and Pavement Technologies segments are unified by unique technologies, leading market positions, and intellectual property that create a sustainable competitive advantage.
quotes: We believe our two business segments are unified by very strong core competencies, including unique technologies that incorporate deep technical expertise on highly engineered materials, leading market positions, and intellectual property, all of which creates a sustainable competitive advantage for Ingevity.

competitive_position.claim: Across its reportable segments, Ingevity describes itself as a leader in adding value to renewable materials, with automotive activated carbon products recovering 8 million gallons of gasoline daily and asphalt emulsifiers enabling pavement recycling that reuses up to 100 percent of existing materials.
quotes: Throughout our Performance Materials, Performance Chemicals, and Advanced Polymer Technologies reportable segments, we are a leader in adding value to products made from renewable materials and in derivatizing technologies that impart desirable environmental benefits in their use.
Our automotive activated carbon products improve the air we breathe by recovering 8 million gallons of gasoline daily.
Our asphalt emulsifiers enable pavement recycling that reuses up to 100 percent of existing materials to create longer-lasting roads.

competitive_position.claim: Ingevity relies on global patents, trademarks, closely guarded trade secrets, and proprietary manufacturing know-how—supporting Evotherm Warm Mix Asphalt, caprolactone, and Performance Materials technologies—to maintain technology leadership and its competitive edge.
quotes: Protection of intellectual property, including patents, closely guarded trade secrets, and highly proprietary manufacturing know-how, as well as other proprietary rights, is critical to maintaining our technology leadership and competitive edge.
Our Evotherm® Warm Mix Asphalt technology is supported by numerous global patents and trademarks.
Additionally, our caprolactone and related technologies are supported by numerous global patents and trademarks, as well as proprietary manufacturing and technical know-how.

competitive_position.claim: Performance Materials demonstrates resilient earnings power, generating $606.9 million in net sales and a 53.8 percent Segment EBITDA margin in 2025 despite automotive industry disruptions, and $154.1 million in net sales with a 54.1% Segment EBITDA margin in the third quarter of 2026.
quotes: Sales of $606.9 million dollars were in line with the prior year, which is a strong result given that 2024 was a record year for the business.
Despite this, Segment EBITDA margin remained strong at 53.8 percent.

Performance Materials net sales remained strong and nearly flat to prior year at $154.1 million as resilient North American demand, supported by continued consumer preference for hybrid vehicles, and higher non-auto filtration sales driven primarily by pricing, offset lower volumes from softness in automotive applications in China and Europe.
Segment EBITDA margin remained strong at 54.1%, consistent with the prior year, demonstrating the resilient earnings power of the segment.

competitive_position.claim: Favorable pricing and sales mix contributed $29.3 million in the first nine months of 2026 and $12.8 million in the third quarter of 2026 across the company, while Advanced Polymer Technologies grew third-quarter 2026 net sales 18% to $45.0 million on higher pricing and mix toward higher-value derivative products.
quotes: The Net sales decrease of $28.0 million in 2026 was driven by a volume decrease of $40.4 million (twelve percent) and unfavorable foreign currency exchange of $0.4 million (zero percent), partially offset by favorable pricing and sales mix of $12.8 million (four percent).

The Net sales decrease of $35.3 million in 2026 was driven by a volume decrease of $68.2 million (seven percent), partially offset by favorable pricing and sales mix of $29.3 million (three percent) and favorable foreign currency exchange of $3.6 million (zero percent).

Advanced Polymer Technologies net sales increased 18% to $45.0 million driven by higher pricing, including a price surcharge to offset increased input costs, and favorable mix toward higher-value derivative products.
Segment EBITDA margin was 26.0%, down 280 basis points as pricing surcharges helped to recover higher input costs, but carried little to no incremental margin.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1, P3, P4, and P6
competitive_position.claim: Ingevity has exited lower-margin and more cyclical businesses—completing the divestiture of its North Charleston CTO refinery and most of its industrial specialties product line in January 2026, selling its road markings product line for $63.2 million in April 2026, and advancing a potential sale of Advanced Polymer Technologies—to concentrate on Performance Materials and Pavement Technologies.
quotes: On September 4, 2025, we announced the agreement to sell the North Charleston crude tall oil refinery and the majority of the industrial specialties product line, and on January 1, 2026, the announced sale was completed.
New Ingevity will be comprised of two attractive businesses aligned around strong core competencies, with superior and consistent profitability: Performance Materials and Pavement Technologies.
On April 15, 2026, we completed the sale of our former Performance Chemicals' road markings product line to PPG Industries Inc. (the "Disposition").

We received all-cash proceeds of $63.2 million, inclusive of preliminary traditional working capital adjustments, and recorded an incremental loss of $3.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, which resulted in a gain of $5.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.
We also continue to advance the sale of Advanced Polymer Technologies, however, the timing of an announced agreement may extend into early 2027.

competitive_position.claim: Performance Materials faces technological substitution threats from competing activated carbon and honeycomb manufacturers, automotive OEMs using sealed fuel tanks that generally do not require extruded honeycombs, and rising electric and hydrogen fuel cell vehicle adoption reducing internal combustion engine demand.
quotes: In the Performance Materials segment, there is competition from other activated carbon and honeycomb manufacturers.

While sealed tank fuel systems generally require an increased sized pelleted activated carbon canister to deal with refueling emissions, in most cases, they do not use an extruded honeycomb to meet current U.S. and California regulations.
A reduction in the sales of vehicles with internal combustion engines would reduce demand for our activated carbon automotive products.
If we are unable to develop products for all-electric and hydrogen fuel cell vehicles or grow sales fast enough, our business and results of operations could be adversely impacted.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 and P3 (counter in P6)
competitive_position.claim: Advanced Polymer Technologies faces threats from other caprolactone manufacturers including new market entrants, increased China competition, and substitute monomers, thermoplastics, and polyols whose pricing is influenced by oil prices, contributing to a $183.8 million goodwill impairment in 2025.
quotes: In the Advanced Polymer Technologies segment, there is competition from other caprolactone manufacturers, including new market entrants.
Other monomers, thermoplastics, and polyols compete with our caprolactone-based products.
The price for our products is impacted by the prices of competitive substitutes which are influenced by oil prices as well as other supply and demand factors.

The Net sales decrease of $32.5 million was driven primarily by the APT reportable segment as continued weak industrial demand, indirect tariff impacts negatively impacted customer end markets demand and increased China competition pressured sales.
As a result, we recorded a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $183.8 million, representing all of the goodwill associated with the APT reporting unit.

competitive_position.claim: With approximately 43 percent of 2025 sales outside the U.S. across approximately 70 countries, Ingevity faces margin and competitive-position threats from U.S. tariffs and retaliatory measures, most notably from China, that could advantage local competitors.
quotes: In 2025, sales to customers outside of the U.S. made up approximately 43 percent of our total sales, and we sell our products to customers in approximately 70 countries.

The retaliatory tariff measures imposed by China, if not unwound, may significantly lower our margin on Performance Materials and Performance Chemicals products sold from the United States into China if we are unable to pass these costs onto our customers.
Reciprocal tariffs from China and other trading partners could impact our competitive position compared to local competitors and other companies not subject to the same restrictions.

competitive_position.claim: Ingevity's intellectual property moat is exposed to invalidation, circumvention, and misappropriation risks—particularly at manufacturing operations in China—and patent enforcement triggered BASF antitrust counterclaims in the Delaware Proceeding resulting in a $28.3 million jury verdict trebled to $85.0 million.
quotes: Our patents and other intellectual property rights may be challenged, invalidated, circumvented, and rendered unenforceable or otherwise compromised.

For instance, we manufacture some of our products in China where we may be at a greater risk of a third party misappropriating our intellectual property despite the foregoing policies, procedures and agreements.

On September 15, 2021, a jury in the lawsuit filed by the Company against BASF Corporation for patent infringement in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware (the "Delaware Proceeding") issued a verdict in favor of BASF on certain counterclaims filed by BASF in the Delaware Proceeding.
The jury awarded BASF damages of approximately $28.3 million, which will be trebled under U.S. antitrust law to approximately $85.0 million when the court enters judgment.

competitive_position.claim: Sales to Ingevity's ten largest customers accounted for 41 percent of total sales in 2025, with no customer exceeding 10 percent, and large-customer relationships rely primarily on individual purchase orders that buyers can terminate at any time with little or no recourse.
quotes: Sales to the Company's ten largest customers (across all three segments) accounted for 41 percent of total sales for 2025.
No customer accounted for more than 10 percent of total sales for 2025.
With some exceptions, our business with those large customers is based primarily upon individual purchase orders.
As such, our customers could cease buying our products from us at any time, for any reason, with little or no recourse.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2, P3, and P6
competitive_position.claim: Pavement Technologies is heavily dependent on government infrastructure spending, faced competitive pricing pressure in Road Markings prior to a $109.3 million asset impairment in 2025 and its 2026 divestiture, and in the third quarter of 2026 saw crude-oil-driven asphalt inflation pressure demand as Segment EBITDA declined $7.3 million to $19.6 million.
quotes: A significant portion of our customers' revenues in our pavement technologies is derived from contracts with various foreign and U.S. governmental agencies, and therefore, when government spending is reduced, our customers' demand for our products is similarly reduced.
Road Markings product line continued to experience price pressure from competition, although volumes grew slightly.
As a result, we recorded a non-cash impairment charge of $109.3 million.
Persistently higher asphalt costs, driven by crude oil inflation, continued to increase project costs for our customers, pressuring demand and limiting sales growth.
Segment EBITDA was $19.6 million, down $7.3 million.

competitive_position.claim: Ingevity's supply reliability faces threats from limited availability of raw materials such as lignin and TOFA, single-site manufacturing of key products including extruded honeycomb and caprolactone, and dependence on co-located third-party utility providers—including at Warrington, U.K., where the provider discontinued most of its own plant operations.
quotes: For example, lignin and TOFA are in limited supply and if we are unable to secure a sufficient amount of lignin or TOFA on a cost-effective basis we could suffer disruption to our pavement technologies product line, which could negatively impact our financial results and our results of operations.

In certain cases, we have products, such as our extruded honeycomb, caprolactone, pavement preservation products, road construction products, pavement reconstruction and recycling products, that are only made at a single site, such as our Waynesboro, Georgia Performance Materials plant, North Charleston Performance Chemicals plant and Warrington, U.K. APT plant.

The third party provider of critical and non-critical services at our location in Warrington, United Kingdom has discontinued most of its operations at its Warrington, United Kingdom plant, but continues to provide services to us.
